traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Enforces that @story annotations reference existing story files. - Uses context.cwd (with fallback to process.cwd) and configurable storyDirectories to resolve paths, matching the story’s path-resolution guidance. - Uses hasValidExtension to enforce `.story.md` by default (configurable via requireStoryExtension). - Delegates path normalization and existence checks to normalizeStoryPath from src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts. - Applies security checks via performSecurityValidations and project-boundary checks via handleProjectBoundaryForExistence (src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts). - Provides clear messageIds and messages: fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError.
- Utilities: src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): builds candidate paths relative to cwd and configured directories (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - fileExistStatusCache and __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(): caches FS results and allows resetting for tests (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - checkSingleCandidate(), getStoryExistence(), storyExists(), normalizeStoryPath(): - Wrap fs.existsSync/statSync in try/catch; never throw. - Distinguish statuses: "exists", "missing", "fs-error" (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - enforceProjectBoundary(): ensures resolved candidates/matchedPath stay within project root (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, isTraversalUnsafe, hasValidExtension, isUnsafeStoryPath: implement security/extension constraints (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION).
- Helpers: src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - analyzeCandidateBoundaries() and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(): centralize boundary logic and call reportInvalidPath when candidates or matchedPath are outside project (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - performSecurityValidations(): validates absolute paths (respecting allowAbsolutePaths) and path traversal; reports invalidPath when unsafe (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION).
Tests (Story-specific): tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - File header references story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md and requirements including REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" RuleTester suite: - Valid: - [REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid story file reference using docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md. - [REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension. - [REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix. - Invalid: - Missing file → messageId: fileMissing, data.path set appropriately (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION). - Wrong extension → messageId: invalidExtension (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION for extension rule). - Path traversal ../outside.story.md → messageId: invalidPath (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Absolute path /etc/passwd.story.md with allowAbsolutePaths default (false) → invalidPath (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Configurable paths: - configurablePathsTester: validates storyDirectories allowing bare filename 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md to resolve from docs/stories (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - allowAbsolutePathsTester: same absolute path is valid when allowAbsolutePaths: true, and invalid when false (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - relaxedExtensionTester: requireStoryExtension: false accepts a .md file and does not emit invalidExtension (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Project boundaries and external directories: - projectBoundaryTester and subsequent tests ensure storyDirectories outside the project cannot make external stories valid; invalidPath is reported (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Additional tests in "Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" confirm: - storyDirectories used in resolution without crashes. - Absolute paths inside project accepted when allowAbsolutePaths: true. - Misconfigured external directories still yield invalidPath diagnostics. - requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md files without invalidExtension. - Error handling tests in "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)": - storyExists returns false, does not throw when fs.existsSync and fs.statSync throw EACCES (simulating permission issues) (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - storyExists returns false, does not throw when fs.statSync throws EIO and existsSync is true (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - Rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws and existsSync is true, including error code in data.error (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, user-facing diagnostics). - Rule reports fileAccessError when existsSync/statSync throw EACCES, again with error message data (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING).
Integration & Documentation: - src/index.ts: - Lists "valid-story-reference" in RULE_NAMES and loads it dynamically as part of the plugin. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES includes "traceability/valid-story-reference": "error" and both recommended and strict configs are built from this (ensures integration with flat-config ESLint usage). - README.md: - Mentions `traceability/valid-story-reference`: "Validates that `@story` references point to existing story files." (high-level user story alignment). - user-docs/api-reference.md, section "traceability/valid-story-reference": - Describes the rule as checking that file paths in @story annotations point to existing story markdown files. - Documents options: storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension, with example configuration (matches story’s configuration example).
Test execution: - `npm test -- --verbose` run in this assessment session. - Output shows: PASS tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts (along with all other suites) and an overall summary: 35 test suites passed, 266 tests passed.
traceability.notes: The story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION defines requirements for validating @story file references: existence, path resolution, security, project boundaries, configurability, performance, error handling, and user-facing clarity. The implementation provides an ESLint rule `traceability/valid-story-reference` plus supporting utilities and helpers that: - Parse @story annotations from comments and extract paths (REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION). - Resolve paths using context.cwd (or process.cwd) and configurable storyDirectories (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Enforce the .story.md extension by default, with a configurable exception via requireStoryExtension (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Prevent unsafe absolute paths and path traversal, and ensure no candidate/matched path falls outside project boundaries (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Use cached filesystem checks with explicit cache reset for tests (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - Differentiate between missing files and filesystem/IO errors, surfacing dedicated fileAccessError diagnostics with clear messages and error details, while never throwing from rule code (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, User Experience criteria). Tests directly reference this story and its requirement IDs and cover happy paths, misconfigurations, permission/IO errors, project boundary breaches, and configuration options. The rule is exported, part of the plugin’s recommended/strict presets, and documented in the user API reference with the same options described in the story. All tests pass under Jest CI. Collectively, this provides strong, concrete evidence that all acceptance criteria and requirements for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are fully implemented and working as specified.
